addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

attachment.content:
- graphify: Use for any question about a codebase, its architecture, file relationships, or project content — especially when graphify-out/ exists, where the question should be treated as a graphify query first. Turns any input (code, docs, papers, images, videos) into a persistent knowledge graph with god nodes, community detection, and query/path/explain tools.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

---

## Project Overview

This is **Memos** (`github.com/usememos/memos`), an open-source, self-hosted note-taking (memo) application. It is written in **Go** (module at `/bench/home/work/go.mod`) with a **React/TypeScript** frontend (in `web/`). The backend is a single Go binary exposing both **gRPC** and **REST** APIs (via gRPC-Gateway and ConnectRPC). It supports three database backends: **SQLite**, **MySQL**, and **PostgreSQL**.

### Top-level structure:

| Directory | Purpose |
|-----------|---------|
| `cmd/memos/` | CLI entry point (Cobra command) |
| `server/` | HTTP/gRPC server, routers, auth, SSE, MCP |
| `store/` | **Data layer** -- entity types, Store facade, Driver interface, DB implementations, migrations |
| `proto/` | Protobuf definitions (API v1 services + store-level messages), generated Go code |
| `internal/` | Internal packages (AI, email, filter, storage/S3, markdown, scheduler, etc.) |
| `web/` | React frontend |
| `docs/` | Documentation |
| `scripts/` | Utility scripts |

---

## Data Layer Location

The data layer is split across two directories:

1. **`/bench/home/work/store/`** -- The Go store package. Contains the `Store` struct (facade), the `Driver` interface, entity struct definitions, and CRUD methods. Database-specific implementations live in `store/db/{sqlite,mysql,postgres}/`.

2. **`/bench/home/work/proto/store/`** -- Protobuf message definitions for structured payloads stored as JSON in the database (e.g., `MemoPayload`, `AttachmentPayload`, `UserSetting`, `InstanceSetting`, `IdentityProvider`, `InboxMessage`). Generated Go code is in `proto/gen/store/`.

---

## Complete List of Persistent Entity Types

### Database Tables (from `store/migration/sqlite/LATEST.sql`)

There are **11 database tables**:

| Table | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `system_setting` | Instance-wide key/value settings |
| `user` | User accounts |
| `user_setting` | Per-user settings (key/value with JSON) |
| `memo` | Memos (the core content unit) |
| `memo_relation` | Relationships between memos (reference, comment) |
| `attachment` | File attachments linked to memos |
| `idp` | Identity providers (OAuth2 SSO) |
| `inbox` | Inbox notifications |
| `reaction` | Reactions on content |
| `memo_share` | Share grants for memos (bearer token access) |
| `user_identity` | Linkage between external identity subjects and local users |

### Go Entity Structs (in `store/` package)

Each entity has a primary struct plus Find/Update/Delete companion structs:

1. **User** -- `/bench/home/work/store/user.go`
   - `User` (fields: ID, RowStatus, CreatedTs, UpdatedTs, Username, Role, Email, Nickname, PasswordHash, AvatarURL, Description)
   - `UpdateUser`, `FindUser`, `DeleteUser`
   - `Role` type (enum: `ADMIN`, `USER`)

2. **Memo** -- `/bench/home/work/store/memo.go`
   - `Memo` (fields: ID, UID, RowStatus, CreatorID, CreatedTs, UpdatedTs, Content, Visibility, Pinned, Payload, ParentUID)
   - `UpdateMemo`, `FindMemo`, `FindMemoPayload`, `DeleteMemo`
   - `Visibility` type (enum: `PUBLIC`, `PROTECTED`, `PRIVATE`)

3. **Attachment** -- `/bench/home/work/store/attachment.go`
   - `Attachment` (fields: ID, UID, CreatorID, CreatedTs, UpdatedTs, Filename, Blob, Type, Size, StorageType, Reference, Payload, MemoID, MemoUID)
   - `UpdateAttachment`, `FindAttachment`, `DeleteAttachment`

4. **MemoRelation** -- `/bench/home/work/store/memo_relation.go`
   - `MemoRelation` (fields: MemoID, RelatedMemoID, Type)
   - `FindMemoRelation`, `DeleteMemoRelation`
   - `MemoRelationType` type (enum: `REFERENCE`, `COMMENT`)

5. **MemoShare** -- `/bench/home/work/store/memo_share.go`
   - `MemoShare` (fields: ID, UID, MemoID, CreatorID, CreatedTs, ExpiresTs)
   - `FindMemoShare`, `DeleteMemoShare`

6. **IdentityProvider** -- `/bench/home/work/store/idp.go`
   - `IdentityProvider` (fields: ID, UID, Name, Type, IdentifierFilter, Config)
   - `FindIdentityProvider`, `UpdateIdentityProvider`, `DeleteIdentityProvider`
   - `UpdateIdentityProviderV1` (extended update with protobuf config)

7. **Inbox** -- `/bench/home/work/store/inbox.go`
   - `Inbox` (fields: ID, CreatedTs, SenderID, ReceiverID, Status, Message)
   - `UpdateInbox`, `FindInbox`, `DeleteInbox`
   - `InboxStatus` type (enum: `UNREAD`, `ARCHIVED`)

8. **Reaction** -- `/bench/home/work/store/reaction.go`
   - `Reaction` (fields: ID, CreatedTs, CreatorID, ContentID, ReactionType)
   - `FindReaction`, `DeleteReaction`

9. **UserSetting** -- `/bench/home/work/store/user_setting.go`
   - `UserSetting` (fields: UserID, Key, Value)
   - `FindUserSetting`, `DeleteUserSetting`
   - `RefreshTokenQueryResult`, `PATQueryResult` (query result types)

10. **UserIdentity** -- `/bench/home/work/store/user_identity.go`
    - `UserIdentity` (fields: ID, UserID, Provider, ExternUID, CreatedTs, UpdatedTs)
    - `FindUserIdentity`, `DeleteUserIdentity`

11. **InstanceSetting** -- `/bench/home/work/store/instance_setting.go`
    - `InstanceSetting` (fields: Name, Value, Description)
    - `FindInstanceSetting`, `DeleteInstanceSetting`

12. **DeleteUserResult** -- `/bench/home/work/store/user_delete.go`
    - `DeleteUserResult` (fields: Attachments, UserSettingKeys) -- aggregated result from cascading user deletion

### Shared Types (in `store/` package)

- **RowStatus** -- `/bench/home/work/store/common.go` -- enum: `NORMAL`, `ARCHIVED`

### Authentication Config Types (in `store/` package)

- **AuthenticationConfigState** -- `/bench/home/work/store/auth_config.go`
- **AuthenticationConfigMutation** -- `/bench/home/work/store/auth_config.go`

### Deployment Config Types (in `store/` package)

- **deploymentConfiguration** (unexported) -- `/bench/home/work/store/store.go` -- holds file-backed identity providers and instance settings

### Protobuf-Defined Payload/Setting Messages (in `proto/store/`)

These are serialized to JSON and stored inside the database columns of the entity tables above:

- **MemoPayload** (with nested Property, Location) -- `/bench/home/work/proto/store/memo.proto`
- **AttachmentPayload** (with nested S3Object), **MotionMedia** -- `/bench/home/work/proto/store/attachment.proto`
- **AttachmentStorageType** enum -- `/bench/home/work/proto/store/attachment.proto`
- **UserSetting** (protobuf version, with Key enum) -- `/bench/home/work/proto/store/user_setting.proto`
- **GeneralUserSetting**, **TagsUserSetting**, **UserTagMetadata** -- `/bench/home/work/proto/store/user_setting.proto`
- **RefreshTokensUserSetting** (with RefreshToken, ClientInfo) -- `/bench/home/work/proto/store/user_setting.proto`
- **PersonalAccessTokensUserSetting** (with PersonalAccessToken) -- `/bench/home/work/proto/store/user_setting.proto`
- **ShortcutsUserSetting** (with Shortcut) -- `/bench/home/work/proto/store/user_setting.proto`
- **WebhooksUserSetting** (with Webhook) -- `/bench/home/work/proto/store/user_setting.proto`
- **InstanceSetting** (protobuf version, with InstanceSettingKey enum) -- `/bench/home/work/proto/store/instance_setting.proto`
- **InstanceBasicSetting**, **InstanceGeneralSetting**, **InstanceCustomProfile** -- `/bench/home/work/proto/store/instance_setting.proto`
- **InstanceStorageSetting**, **StorageS3Config** -- `/bench/home/work/proto/store/instance_setting.proto`
- **InstanceMemoRelatedSetting** -- `/bench/home/work/proto/store/instance_setting.proto`
- **InstanceTagsSetting**, **InstanceTagMetadata** -- `/bench/home/work/proto/store/instance_setting.proto`
- **InstanceNotificationSetting** (with EmailSetting) -- `/bench/home/work/proto/store/instance_setting.proto`
- **InstanceAISetting**, **AIProviderConfig**, **TranscriptionConfig** -- `/bench/home/work/proto/store/instance_setting.proto`
- **IdentityProvider** (protobuf version), **IdentityProviderConfig**, **OAuth2Config**, **FieldMapping** -- `/bench/home/work/proto/store/idp.proto`
- **InboxMessage** (with MemoCommentPayload, MemoMentionPayload) -- `/bench/home/work/proto/store/inbox.proto`

### Driver Interface

The `Driver` interface at `/bench/home/work/store/driver.go` defines the contract that all three database backends (SQLite, MySQL, PostgreSQL) must implement. It lists CRUD methods for all 11 entity types listed above.
